transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
Lately I keep hearing things that no one else seems to hear, and it’s starting to really bother me at work and at home. It's just getting very hard to ignore, and I'm not sure what to do about it.
How long have you been hearing these things—has it been less than a month, one to six months, or longer than six months?
It's been going on steadily for about three months now, so it falls in that one-to-six-month range. It hasn't just been a fleeting thing, but a constant, daily issue for me during this time.
Have you had any periods of feeling completely back to normal, or has this been going on continuously for the entire three months?

No, I haven't had any breaks where I felt completely back to normal. It has been a steady, continuous problem every single day for the entire three months. It's really wearing me down because it just doesn't seem to let up.
Besides hearing things, have you also had any unusual beliefs, disorganized thoughts or speech, or felt confused or very disorganized in your behavior?

I don't think I have any unusual beliefs, but I’ve definitely noticed some strange behaviors, especially at work. Sometimes I'll just freeze in place holding a can in midair or staring at the scanner, or feel this strong urge to tap items three times before bagging them. It happens even when there's a line of customers waiting, which I know looks really odd.
During these three months, have you also had any major mood changes, like feeling very depressed, unusually energized, needing much less sleep, or having racing thoughts?
No, I haven't had any major mood swings like that. I certainly haven't felt unusually energized or had racing thoughts. If anything, my mood has just felt very flat and quiet lately.
Have you ever had any similar symptoms before this three-month period, or is this the first time this has happened?

The voice and the freezing at the register are definitely new and have only been happening for the last three months. However, other changes, like losing interest in my hobbies and pulling away from my family, have actually been building up for a little over two years now.
Have the low mood, loss of interest, or withdrawal happened for most of the same time as the hearing voices, or did they start separately and only occur outside the psychotic symptoms?

They started separately, way before the voices did. The loss of interest and pulling away from my family have been building for over two years now, since my daughter moved out. The voice and the issues at the register are much more recent and have only been a steady problem for the last three months.
Have the hearing voices and the freezing/staring happened only during times when you felt depressed, or have they also occurred when your mood was otherwise normal?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it in terms of my mood. I've mostly just felt disconnected and unmotivated rather than specifically depressed when these things happen. It seems like the voices and the freezing just happen regardless of how I'm feeling.
Have there been any times when you had the voices or freezing/staring without also having a major mood episode, such as feeling very depressed or unusually energized for at least a couple of weeks?

I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme mood changes, like feeling severely depressed or unusually energized, at all. The voices and the freezing just seem to happen on their own, without any big shifts in my mood. It has just been a constant, flat feeling rather than any major highs or lows.
Have there ever been any periods of at least two weeks when your mood was very depressed or unusually energized, and did the voices or freezing happen only during those mood episodes?
No, I haven't ever experienced periods of being extremely depressed or unusually energized like that. The voices and freezing moments don't seem tied to any specific mood swings at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 3-month continuous psychotic syndrome with auditory hallucinations and bizarre/odd motor behavior, causing clear impairment at work and home. Mood episodes are absent, and the psychotic symptoms are not confined to a depressive or manic episode. Although the duration is only three months (which is shorter than the typical 6-month requirement for schizophrenia), the overall presentation is most consistent with a schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic disorder, with schizophrenia as the leading candidate among the provided options.
